mechanism: Raloxifene is a substrate for glucuronidation and biliary excretion, while oxybutynin is metabolized via CYP3A4; both drugs have anticholinergic properties that may be additive.
action: Monitor for increased anticholinergic side effects (constipation, urinary retention, dry mouth, confusion) and consider dose adjustment or alternative antimuscarinic agent if adverse effects occur.
